first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction can improve early adoption. A small guarded test is preferable to promotional pricing because it addresses the current funnel deterioration while avoiding margin erosion and potential low-quality acquisition. The test should monitor qualified activation and downstream revenue, not just completion rate.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding, since completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, and the verified record shows a durable improvement in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. Do not lead with signup simplification: although it lifted SMB activation and qualified revenue, it also reduced 30-day retention by 1% and was not replicated beyond SMB. Measure qualified activation, time-to-value, 30-day retention, and qualified revenue to ensure the funnel lift translates into sustainable value.
